# Lexical-relation correction pass — M7 measurement (Contract v1 rev 3 → rev 4)

*Generated by `python -m identity_resolution.calibration.lexical_pass report`; a test regenerates it from `before_rev3.json` and `after_rev4.json`. Draft contract, NOT frozen, `binding: false`. Nothing here touched production, the DB, mappings, R6/R7, migrations, engine wiring, PR #201, adoption binding or the freeze state.*

## 1. What changed (owner decision 2026-10-11, `od_lexical_relation_correction`)

| Rule | Policy key | Value |
|---|---|---|
| FUZZY never pairs a token that contains a digit | `lexical.fuzzy_token.allow_tokens_with_digits` | `false` (new) |
| SIBLING needs a distinctive shared token | `lexical.distinctive_token.required_for_relations` | `[SIBLING]` (new) |
| …distinctive = at least this long | `lexical.distinctive_token.min_length` | `3` (proposal, pending) |
| …and not purely numeric | `lexical.distinctive_token.exclude_numeric` | `true` (proposal, pending) |
| …and not descriptor vocabulary (body, powertrain, trim, generation, market) | `lexical.distinctive_token.non_distinctive` | 5 classes (proposal, pending) |
| …and not a descriptor shape (`4x2`, `V10`, `25hev`, `Gen2`, `Mk4`) | `lexical.distinctive_token.non_distinctive_patterns` | 5 patterns (proposal, pending) |
| Honda-scoped model synonyms | `aliases.model` entry `honda_model_synonyms` (`brands: [Honda]`) | `Jazz` ↔ `Fit`, `Stepwagon` ↔ `Step WGN` |

No model is named in the evaluator. `V`, `CX`, `GR`, `RS`, `HR` fall out of the length floor, `30` out of the numeric rule, `4x2`/`V10` out of the patterns. `AMG` has three letters and is a performance-trim label, so it is the one entry the descriptor vocabulary (class `trim`) has to carry; the owner can strike it. `SPEC §5.3`, `§5.4`, invariant `I19`, taxonomy `NAME-14`…`NAME-17`, 54 new corpus cases.

## 2. How it was measured

* **Populations.** `ice_ice`: every pair of Ice groups with the same Ice brand string (1,200 groups). `ice_tdr`: every Ice group against every TDR model in its v1 candidate pool. Both are name pairs; no series is involved.
* **Before** is the unchanged rev 3 evaluator, re-derived live by `rev3_rules()` (the three rules switched back in the shared policy object); a test checks it reproduces `before_rev3.json` exactly. **After** is the current evaluator. Nothing else differs between the two runs.
* **Independent oracle.** The diagnostic columns (“FUZZY across a digit token”, “SIBLING resting only on non-distinctive tokens”) come from an oracle in this module that restates the owner's wording from the policy vocabulary and does not call the evaluator's relation code; a test requires both to agree (after the change both diagnostics are 0 for every remaining pair).
* **Independent of PR #201.** Its stand-in and its numbers were not used. Its structural-conflict wording was quoted: a duplicate (`EQUAL*`/`FUZZY`) conflicts both groups, `SUBJECT_FINER` the finer group, `SIBLING` both; the stand-in used a 4-character FUZZY floor, the contract uses 6, so the two FUZZY counts are not comparable and are not compared.

## 7. Honda synonyms

Ice × Ice: `honda-honda-fit|honda-jazz`, `honda-honda-stepwagon|honda-step-wgn`. Ice × TDR: `honda-honda-stepwagon|honda.step_wgn`. The TDR catalog extract has no `Jazz` or `Fit` model, so `honda-jazz` and `honda-honda-fit` still have no candidate; they are now recognised as one vehicle in two Ice groups. `honda-honda-stepwagon` reaches the existing `honda.step_wgn` by name only (its series is not strong), as a PROPOSE that conflicts with `honda-step-wgn`'s AUTO; no AUTO was added.

## 8. What this pass does not fix (observations, for the owner)

* **Containment on descriptors is unchanged.** `SUBJECT_COARSER`/`SUBJECT_FINER` pairs whose smaller side is all descriptor tokens: Ice × Ice 15 + 16, Ice × TDR 7 + 19. The owner asked only for FUZZY and SIBLING; `required_for_relations` can list them with no code change.
* **Remaining FUZZY.** Ice × TDR: `KIA|CANIVAL|kia.carnival`, `TOYOTA|COMUTER|toyota.commuter` (genuine typos). Ice × Ice keeps 7: `CANIVAL`/`kia-carnival` (a typo), `foton-etunland`/`foton-tunland` (an electric variant, arguably a different model) and five Toyota catalog codes that differ in one *letter* (`JEXGBT`/`JEXVBT`, `PRMDHT`/`PRMSHT`, `GEXEGT`/`GEXGGT`). They are outside the stated rule (no digit in the differing token) and are still FUZZY, a name-only PROPOSE candidate.
* **Residual siblings.** A shared three-letter engine/technology word such as `cgi` (`C180 CGI Saloon` / `E200 CGI Saloon`) is distinctive under the length rule. It stays a SIBLING; both relations veto, so no outcome depends on it.
* **Synonyms are whole-name pairs.** `Jazz Hybrid` ≠ `Fit Hybrid`, and `Step Wagon` (two words) ≠ `Step WGN`; the first is a documented corpus case, neither is a wish.
* **Descriptor vocabulary is a proposal.** Each class and each pattern is pinned by corpus cases; individual words are not (the mutation sweep leaves 80 single words individually undetected). A test requires every word to be one normalized token so none can be inert by typo.

## 9. The AUTO-monotonicity invariant (I19)

`tests/identity_resolution/test_ir_lexical_invariants.py` pins, on the corpus (always) and on this snapshot (when the archived package is present):

1. Over every name pair, a tightened relation is never more permissive than the rev 3 relation (FUZZY → CONTRADICTION/SIBLING, SIBLING → CONTRADICTION; EQUAL* unchanged).
2. The only new `EQUAL*` pairs are the Honda synonyms.
3. Over every resolve case and every real subject, AUTO(after) ⊆ AUTO(before) ∪ {subjects whose best candidate is a synonym}; a non-AUTO subject never becomes AUTO through a demotion. Measured: AUTO 69 → 69, same set.
4. `before_rev3.json` and `after_rev4.json` are what the code produces today, and this report is what they render to.
